user.title: Which house is this?
user.description: The name is what this house is called everywhere else. The address is left blank to use the site name under {zone}.

data_description.hostname: Leave blank and it is worked out from the site name.
data_description.device_pin: The common PIN Crestron Home set on this house's devices. Used for the amplifiers, the touch panels and the add-on APIs.

crestron.title: The Crestron Home processor
crestron.description: The processor is checked before this form is accepted. Tick Skip if this house has no processor, or it is not on the network yet.

data.skip: Skip - set Crestron Home up later

data_description.crestron_token: From the processor's web interface, under Installer Settings.

cloudflare.title: Remote access
cloudflare.description:
A tunnel called this is created in Cloudflare, pointed at Home Assistant, and {hostname} is made to resolve to it. Nobody has to open a browser to authorise it.

Fleet Cloudflare account on this box: {account}

data_description.cf_tunnel_name: Must be unique across the Cloudflare account. The site name is the usual choice.

cloudflare_account.title: Cloudflare account
cloudflare_account.description: The API token needs Cloudflare Tunnel edit on the account and DNS edit on the zone. Leave the token blank to set this house up without remote access.

data_description.cf_zone: The domain the address lives under, for example bav.homes.

addons.title: What to install
addons.description: Each one is installed, configured for this house from what you have already entered, and started. Installing builds the add-on on this box, which on a Raspberry Pi takes a few minutes each.

devices.title: The house's own kit
devices.description:
All optional — leave anything blank that this house does not have, or that is not installed yet. These go straight into the add-ons that need them, so nobody has to paste them in afterwards.

Protect and Access share one UniFi console address.

data_description.unifi_host: The UDM or console, for example 192.168.0.1.
data_description.protect_api_key: Protect app → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations. Not the same thing as the Access token below.
data_description.access_token: A UniFi Access API token, made in the Access application under Settings → Advanced → API Token, with device and door permissions. Not the Protect key — they are different credentials even on the same console, and the Protect key is refused. Needed for door discovery and for unlocking from a panel.
data_description.nax_host: For example 192.168.0.51. Its zones are read off the device afterwards.
data_description.nax_password: Defaults to the common device PIN entered earlier.

error.cannot_connect: Nothing answered at that address. Check the processor is on the network and reachable from Home Assistant.
error.invalid_auth: The processor answered but refused that token.
error.cloudflare_auth: Cloudflare refused those credentials, or the token cannot see that account.
error.bad_site_name: That site name has no letters or digits in it.

abort.single_instance_allowed: This box is already set up as a house. Use the integration's Configure button to change what is installed, or the bav_house.provision action to run commissioning again.

init.title: What to install
init.description: Changing this does not install anything on its own - run the bav_house.provision action afterwards.

provision.name: Commission this house
provision.description: Run commissioning again. Steps that already succeeded are skipped.
